title: Dragon Quest RPG: The Cursed Tree & Chosen Isle Launch on iOS & Android – Gematsu Reveal
body:
Square Enix has unveiled the next installment of its mobile‑first Dragon Quest franchise, announcing **Dragon Quest RPG: The Cursed Tree and the Chosen Isle** for iOS and Android devices. Marketed as “the next adventure in the Dragon Quest series,” the title promises a blend of classic turn‑based combat, expansive exploration, and new narrative threads designed specifically for touch‑screen play. The announcement, made at a digital press event, signals the company’s continued investment in the lucrative mobile gaming segment while attempting to bridge the gap between longtime console fans and a growing audience of smartphone gamers.

The new entry builds on the foundations laid by earlier mobile releases such as *Dragon Quest RPG: The Distant Land* and *Dragon Quest RPG: The Star‑Gazing Planet*. Those titles introduced a hybrid model that combined the series’ signature role‑playing mechanics with gacha‑style character collection and periodic live‑service updates. According to Square Enix’s development team, *The Cursed Tree and the Chosen Isle* will retain the familiar job‑system and party‑building dynamics, but will feature a reworked UI that leverages larger screens and haptic feedback. Players can expect a more fluid navigation experience, with swipe‑based map traversal and tap‑to‑target combat that aims to reduce the “button‑mashing” feel often criticized in earlier mobile adaptations.

Narratively, the game centers on a mysterious, ever‑growing tree whose roots have begun to corrupt the surrounding kingdom, prompting the player’s party to venture to the newly discovered Chosen Isle—a floating archipelago that houses ancient Dragon Quest lore. The storyline is being positioned as a “stand‑alone adventure” that does not require prior knowledge of the series, a strategic move to attract newcomers who might be hesitant to dive into a long‑running franchise. Yet, the developers have hinted at cameo appearances from iconic series staples, such as the Hero of Light and recurring monster designs, to reward veteran fans with familiar touchstones.

From a business perspective, Square Enix’s focus on mobile platforms reflects broader industry trends. The global mobile gaming market is projected to exceed $120 billion this year, with role‑playing games accounting for a substantial share of in‑app purchases. By delivering a premium‑look title that incorporates both free‑to‑play accessibility and optional microtransactions for cosmetic items and character summons, the company hopes to capture a slice of that revenue while preserving the brand’s reputation for quality storytelling. Analysts note that the inclusion of periodic live events, seasonal content, and cross‑promotion with other Square Enix properties could further cement player retention, a critical metric in the competitive mobile arena.

Critics and fans alike will be watching how *The Cursed Tree and the Chosen Isle* balances depth with convenience. While the Dragon Quest series is celebrated for its intricate world‑building and strategic combat, mobile adaptations have sometimes been forced to simplify these elements to accommodate shorter play sessions. Early screenshots suggest a richer visual palette and more detailed character models than previous mobile releases, indicating that the studio may have allocated additional resources to ensure the game feels “console‑worthy” on handheld devices. Moreover, the promised offline mode for certain story chapters could address concerns about connectivity requirements, a frequent pain point for players in regions with unstable internet access.

Looking ahead, the launch of *Dragon Quest RPG: The Cursed Tree and the Chosen Isle* could set a benchmark for how legacy RPG franchises evolve within the mobile ecosystem. If Square Enix succeeds in delivering a compelling experience that satisfies both hardcore enthusiasts and casual gamers, it may inspire other venerable developers to revisit their own catalogues for the smartphone market. The company has yet to disclose a specific release window, but anticipation is already building among the series’ global fanbase. As the line between console and mobile gaming continues to blur, the upcoming title stands as a test case for whether classic role‑playing narratives can thrive on the small screen without compromising the depth that has defined them for decades.
